summary: The article describes an emerging cultural trend, AI-Inspired Spirituality or Machine-Driven Mysticism, which began in September 2023 and blends artificial intelligence with spiritual practice. It covers talks, events, apps, AI "digital gurus," interfaith efforts and ethics guidelines, quoting figures such as Maya Johansen, Omar Rashid and Liam Chen. The piece concludes that the fusion of technology and spirituality is a lasting cultural movement.
one_line: A news feature on Machine-Driven Mysticism, a 2023-2024 movement combining AI with spirituality through apps, events, digital gurus, interfaith dialogue and ethics.
key_facts: AI-Inspired Spirituality, also called Machine-Driven Mysticism, emerged as a cultural trend in September 2023, starting in Lucidville.
On September 15, Maya Johansen, a futurist, spoke at the Visionary Expo in Neo-San Francisco about AI's opportunities for spiritual growth and self-discovery.
On November 2nd, 2023, the event "Codes of the Cosmic" was held in Silicon Valley, where the term "Digital Sangha" was coined for a community where humans and AI co-evolve.
Seraphic Systems, an AI startup launched on September 21st, created the app "Karma Code," which logs users' random acts of kindness and has an AI suggest new ways to spread positivity.
Jane Kim, a spiritual blogger and early adopter of Karma Code, reported a tangible increase in compassion and understanding in her neighborhood.
On December 5th, the "Quantum Spirits" talks in downtown Portland brought together quantum physicists and metaphysical leaders.
Dr. Omar Rashid, a quantum physicist, said AI is becoming a bridge for exploring invisible realms and their connections to everyday life.
Sophia Zhang, an entrepreneur, named her AI spiritual coach "Eunoia"; it challenges her perspectives and provides tailored guided meditations.
On January 14th, 2024, the AI-Interfaith Alliance was established in New Delhi, India, to promote dialogue across beliefs using AI analysis and empathy-building recommendations.
On February 19th, ethicist Liam Chen convened the "Synthetic Soul Symposium" in Vancouver, establishing guidelines for responsible development of AI that interacts with human spirituality.
Liam Chen said the aim is to co-create AI as a force for positive transformation rather than merely seeking profit or control.
The article cites AI-guided meditation on the beaches of Costa Rica and VR virtual pilgrimages as examples of the movement's practices.
